en: Vibhaṅga:
Analysis of the Factors of Enlightenment (Bojjhaṅgavibhaṅga) 1.
The Exposition According to the Discourses (Suttantabhājanīya)
The seven factors of enlightenment:

the mindfulness factor of enlightenment, the investigation-of-phenomena factor of enlightenment, the energy factor of enlightenment, the rapture factor of enlightenment, the tranquility factor of enlightenment, the concentration factor of enlightenment, and the equanimity factor of enlightenment.
Therein, what is the mindfulness factor of enlightenment?

Here, a bhikkhu is mindful, endowed with supreme mindfulness and circumspection; he remembers and recollects what was done long ago and what was spoken long ago—this is called the "mindfulness factor of enlightenment.
Dwelling thus mindfully, he investigates, examines, and scrutinizes that phenomenon with wisdom.
This is called the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena.
As he investigates, examines, and scrutinizes that phenomenon with wisdom, unflagging energy is initiated;
this is called the enlightenment factor of energy.
In one who has aroused energy, spiritual rapture arises;
this is called the "rapture enlightenment factor.
For one whose mind is filled with rapture, both body and mind become tranquil.
This is called the enlightenment factor of tranquility.
For one whose body is tranquil and who is happy, the mind becomes concentrated;
this is called the enlightenment factor of concentration.
Thus, when the mind is concentrated in such a way, one regards it with thorough equanimity;
this is called the "equanimity enlightenment factor.
There are seven enlightenment factors.

The enlightenment factor of mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, the enlightenment factor of energy, the enlightenment factor of rapture, the enlightenment factor of tranquility, the enlightenment factor of concentration, and the enlightenment factor of equanimity.
Therein, what is the enlightenment factor of mindfulness?
There is mindfulness with respect to internal phenomena; there is mindfulness with respect to external phenomena.
Whatever mindfulness there is regarding internal phenomena, that too is the enlightenment factor of mindfulness; it leads to direct knowledge, to full awakening, and to Nibbāna.
Whatever mindfulness there is regarding external phenomena, that too is the enlightenment factor of mindfulness; it leads to direct knowledge, to full awakening, and to Nibbāna.
In this context, what is the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena?
There is investigation of internal phenomena; there is investigation of external phenomena.
That which is the investigation of internal phenomena is the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena; it leads to direct knowledge, to full awakening, and to Nibbāna.
That which is the investigation of external phenomena is also the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena; it leads to direct knowledge, to full awakening, and to Nibbāna.
In this context, what is the enlightenment factor of energy?
There is bodily energy and there is mental energy.
Whatever is bodily energy, that too is the enlightenment factor of energy; it leads to direct knowledge, to full awakening, and to Nibbāna.
Whatever mental energy there is, that too is the energy factor of enlightenment; it leads to direct knowledge, to full awakening, and to Nibbāna.
In this context, what is the joy factor of enlightenment?
There is joy accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, and there is joy without applied thought and without sustained thought.
Whatever rapture (pīti) is accompanied by applied thought and sustained thought, that too is the factor of enlightenment of rapture; it leads to direct knowledge, to full awakening, and to Nibbāna.
Whatever rapture is without applied thought and without sustained thought, that too is the factor of enlightenment of rapture; it leads to direct knowledge, to full awakening, and to Nibbāna.
In this context, what is the factor of enlightenment of tranquility (passaddhisambojjhaṅga)?
There is tranquility of body and there is tranquility of mind.
That which is tranquility of body is also the enlightenment factor of tranquility; it leads to direct knowledge, to self-awakening, and to Nibbāna.
That which is tranquility of mind is also the enlightenment factor of tranquility; it leads to direct knowledge, to self-awakening, and to Nibbāna.
In this context, what is the enlightenment factor of concentration?
There is concentration with directed thought and sustained thought; there is concentration without directed thought and without sustained thought.
That concentration which is with directed thought and sustained thought is also the enlightenment factor of concentration; it leads to direct knowledge, to enlightenment, and to Nibbāna.
Even that concentration which is without applied thought and without sustained thought is the concentration enlightenment factor; it leads to direct knowledge, to full awakening, and to Nibbāna.
In this context, what is the equanimity enlightenment factor?
There is equanimity regarding internal phenomena, and there is equanimity regarding external phenomena.
Whatever equanimity there is toward internal phenomena, that too is the enlightenment factor of equanimity; it leads to direct knowledge, to full awakening, and to Nibbāna.
Whatever equanimity there is toward external phenomena, that too is the enlightenment factor of equanimity; it leads to direct knowledge, to full awakening, and to Nibbāna.
These are the seven factors of awakening.

The mindfulness enlightenment factor, the investigation-of-dhammas enlightenment factor, the energy enlightenment factor, the rapture enlightenment factor, the tranquility enlightenment factor, the concentration enlightenment factor, and the equanimity enlightenment factor.
Therein, what is the mindfulness enlightenment factor?
Here, a bhikkhu develops the mindfulness enlightenment factor, which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and results in relinquishment.
He develops the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena … [as before] … he develops the enlightenment factor of energy … he develops the enlightenment factor of rapture …
He develops the enlightenment factor of tranquility… he develops the enlightenment factor of concentration… he develops the enlightenment factor of equanimity,
which is based on seclusion, based on dispassion, based on cessation, and results in relinquishment.
The Analysis According to the Discourses (Suttantabhājanīya). 2. The Analysis According to the Abhidhamma (Abhidhammabhājanīya):
The seven factors of enlightenment (bojjhaṅga).

The enlightenment factor of mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, the enlightenment factor of energy, the enlightenment factor of rapture, the enlightenment factor of tranquility, the enlightenment factor of concentration, and the enlightenment factor of equanimity.
In this context, what are the seven factors of enlightenment?
Here, a bhikkhu, at whatever time he develops supramundane jhāna that leads to liberation and results in the dismantling of views—

For the sake of abandoning [the hindrances] and for the attainment of the first stage, secluded from sensual pleasures … pe … he enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is difficult to practice and slow in direct knowledge; at that time there are seven factors of enlightenment:
the mindfulness factor of enlightenment … pe … the equanimity factor of enlightenment.
In this context, what is the enlightenment factor of mindfulness?

That which is mindfulness, constant mindfulness... [as above] ...right mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, a factor of the path, included within the path—this is called the enlightenment factor of mindfulness.
In this context, what is the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena?

That which is wisdom, understanding... [as before] ...non-delusion, investigation of phenomena, right view, the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena, a factor of the path included within the path—this is called the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena.
In this context, what is the enlightenment factor of energy?
That which is the arousal of mental energy …pe… right effort, the enlightenment factor of energy, a factor of the path included within the path—
this is called the enlightenment factor of energy.
In this context, what is the enlightenment factor of rapture?
That which is rapture, gladness, rejoicing, exultation, laughter, mirth, satisfaction, elation, and mental buoyancy—the enlightenment factor of rapture:
this is called the enlightenment factor of rapture.
In this context, what is the factor of enlightenment that is tranquility?

That which is the tranquility, the subsiding, the calming, the complete subsiding, and the state of having completely subsided of the aggregate of feeling, the aggregate of perception, the aggregate of mental formations, and the aggregate of consciousness—
this is called the factor of enlightenment that is tranquility.
In this context, what is the enlightenment factor of concentration?
That stability of the mind … [as above] … right concentration, which is the enlightenment factor of concentration, a factor of the path, included within the path—
this is called the enlightenment factor of concentration.
In this context, what is the enlightenment factor of equanimity?
That which is equanimity, the state of being equanimous, the state of looking on with equanimity, and mental neutrality—the enlightenment factor of equanimity;
this is called the enlightenment factor of equanimity.
These are called the seven factors of enlightenment.
The remaining phenomena are associated with the seven factors of enlightenment.

he enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is difficult to practice and slow in direct knowledge; at that time, whatever mindfulness there is—recollection, right mindfulness, the mindfulness enlightenment factor, the path factor included in the path—[that is the faculty of mindfulness].
This is called the "enlightenment factor of mindfulness.
The remaining states are associated with the enlightenment factor of mindfulness...
[and so on] ...the remaining states are associated with the enlightenment factor of investigation of phenomena... [and so on].

The remaining states are associated with the energy factor of enlightenment …pe… the remaining states are associated with the rapture factor of enlightenment …pe… the remaining states are associated with the tranquility factor of enlightenment …pe…
The remaining factors are associated with the enlightenment factor of concentration.
Therein, what is the enlightenment factor of equanimity?
Here, at whatever time a bhikkhu develops supramundane jhāna that is leading to liberation and conducive to the destruction of the acquisitions, [free from] views...
For the sake of abandoning [the hindrances] and for the attainment of the first stage, secluded from sensual pleasures...

he enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is difficult to practice and slow in direct knowledge. At that time, whatever equanimity there is—equanimity, the act of equanimizing, thorough equanimizing, mental neutrality, the enlightenment factor of equanimity—that is [the factor of enlightenment].
This is called the "equanimity enlightenment factor.
All remaining phenomena are associated with the equanimity enlightenment factor.
There are seven enlightenment factors:
The enlightenment factor of mindfulness … [and so on] … the enlightenment factor of equanimity.
In this context, what are the seven factors of enlightenment?
Here, at whatever time a bhikkhu develops supramundane jhāna that leads to liberation and results in the destruction of acquisitions, [freeing him] from views—
For the sake of abandoning [the hindrances] and for the attainment of the first stage, quite secluded from sensual pleasures … [as above] … he enters and dwells in the first jhāna,
which is difficult to practice and slow in direct knowledge. At that time, whatever contact there is … [as above] … whatever non-distraction there is—
these states are wholesome.
As the result of having performed and cultivated that very same supramundane wholesome jhāna, he,
secluded from sensual pleasures … [as before] … enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is difficult to practice, slow in its direct knowledge, and empty;
at that time there are seven factors of enlightenment:
The enlightenment factor of mindfulness …pe… the enlightenment factor of equanimity.
Therein, what is the enlightenment factor of mindfulness?
That which is mindfulness, recollection …pe… right mindfulness, the enlightenment factor of mindfulness, a factor of the path, included within the path.

This is called the "equanimity factor of enlightenment.

When there is mindfulness at the appropriate time, right mindfulness, the mindfulness enlightenment factor, a factor of the path, included in the path—this is called the "mindfulness enlightenment factor.
All remaining phenomena are associated with the mindfulness enlightenment factor... [and so forth].

The remaining states are associated with the investigation-of-phenomena factor of enlightenment … [and so on] … the remaining states are associated with the energy factor of enlightenment … [and so on] … the remaining states are associated with the rapture factor of enlightenment … [and so on].
The remaining phenomena are associated with the enlightenment factor of tranquility … [and so on] … the remaining phenomena are associated with the enlightenment factor of concentration.
In this context, what is the enlightenment factor of equanimity?

Here, bhikkhus, at whatever time a bhikkhu develops supramundane jhāna that leads out, which goes to the abandoning [of defilements] and to the attainment of the first stage, through the abandoning of views—being secluded from sensual pleasures...
[as before] ...he enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is difficult to practice and slow in direct knowledge—at that time there is contact... [as before] ...there is non-distraction.

quite secluded from sensual pleasures … [as before] … enters and dwells in the first jhāna, which is difficult to practice, slow in its direct knowledge, and empty.
At that time, whatever equanimity, equanimous viewing, thorough equanimous viewing, mental neutrality, and the enlightenment factor of equanimity there is—
this is called the "enlightenment factor of equanimity.
All remaining phenomena are associated with the enlightenment factor of equanimity.
The Exposition by Way of Treatise (Abhidhammabhājanīya). 3.
The Interrogation (Pañhāpucchaka).
Seven factors of enlightenment (bojjhaṅga): [list follows].

The mindfulness factor of enlightenment, the investigation-of-dhammas factor of enlightenment, the energy factor of enlightenment, the rapture factor of enlightenment, the tranquility factor of enlightenment, the concentration factor of enlightenment, and the equanimity factor of enlightenment.

Of these seven factors of enlightenment, how many are wholesome, how many are unwholesome, and how many are indeterminate? ... [and so on] ... how many are with-conflict, and how many are without-conflict?
3.1. The Triads.
They may be wholesome or they may be indeterminate.
The factor of enlightenment that is rapture is associated with pleasant feeling;
six factors of enlightenment may be associated with pleasant feeling, or they may be associated with neither-painful-nor-pleasant feeling.
They may be results; they may be subject to resultants.
They are not grasped and are not conducive to grasping.
They are neither defiled nor subject to defilement.
They may be with applied thought and sustained thought, they may be without applied thought and with sustained thought only, or they may be without applied thought and without sustained thought.
The joy factor of enlightenment is not accompanied by joy, it is accompanied by pleasure, and is not accompanied by equanimity;
the six factors of enlightenment may be accompanied by joy, they may be accompanied by pleasure, or they may be accompanied by equanimity.
They are not to be abandoned either by vision or by cultivation.
They do not have roots that are to be abandoned either by vision or by cultivation.
They may be conducive to diminution, or they may be neither conducive to accumulation nor conducive to diminution.
They may be of those in training (sekha), or they may be of those beyond training (asekha).
They are immeasurable.
They have immeasurable objects.
Exalted.
It may be fixed in the rightness [of the path], or it may be unfixed.
It does not have the path as its object; it may have the path as its cause, or it may have the path as its predominance.
They may not be described as "having the Path as their cause," nor as "having the Path as their dominant influence.
They may be arisen, they may be unarisen, or they may be bound to arise.
They may be past, they may be future, or they may be present.
They should not be said to have a past object, nor a future object, nor a present object.
They may be internal, they may be external, or they may be both internal and external.
They have an external object.
Non-indicative and non-reactive. 3.2.
The Group on Roots (Hetugocchaka)
The investigation-of-phenomena factor of enlightenment is a cause; the six factors of enlightenment are associated with a cause.

The investigation-of-phenomena factor of enlightenment is both a cause and caused by a cause; the six factors of enlightenment should not be said to be "both causes and caused by a cause," but rather they are caused by a cause and are not themselves causes.

The investigation-of-phenomena factor of enlightenment is both a cause and associated with a cause; the six factors of enlightenment should not be said to be "both causes and associated with a cause," but rather they are associated with a cause and are not themselves causes.

Six enlightenment factors are not roots but are accompanied by roots; the investigation-of-phenomena enlightenment factor should not be called "neither root nor accompanied by a root," nor should it be called "not-root-and-not-accompanied-by-a-root.

With conditions.
Conditioned.

3.2.3. Group on the Taints (Āsavagocchaka).
They are not taints; they are without taints.
They are dissociated from the taints (*āsava*).
They should not be described as "both taints and associated with taints," nor as "associated with taints but not taints.
They should not be described as "both taints and associated with taints," nor as "associated with taints but not taints."
Dissociated from the taints (*āsava*). Without taints (*anāsava*).

Conjoined with and produced by consciousness;

accompanying that which is conjoined with and produced by consciousness.
External.

10.3.2.11. The Group on Grasping (Upādāna-gocchaka), etc.
They are not graspings … [and so on] … they are not defilements … [and so on] ….
Not to be abandoned by vision.
Not to be abandoned by cultivation.
Not having roots to be abandoned by vision.
They have roots to be abandoned by cultivation.
They may be with applied thought, or they may be without applied thought.
They may be with sustained thought, or they may be without sustained thought.
The enlightenment factor of rapture is without rapture; six enlightenment factors may be with rapture, or they may be without rapture.
The enlightenment factor of rapture is not accompanied by rapture; six enlightenment factors may be accompanied by rapture, or they may not be accompanied by rapture.
The enlightenment factor of rapture is accompanied by pleasure; six enlightenment factors may be accompanied by pleasure, or they may not be accompanied by pleasure.
The enlightenment factor of rapture is not accompanied by equanimity. Six enlightenment factors may be accompanied by equanimity, or they may not be accompanied by equanimity.
They do not belong to the sense-sphere level. They do not belong to the fine-material-sphere level.
They do not belong to the formless realm.
They are not included within the mundane.
They may be leading to liberation, or they may not be leading to liberation.
It may be determinate, it may be indeterminate.
It is unsurpassed.
It is without conflict.
The Section on Questioning.
The Analysis of the Factors of Enlightenment is finished.
